narrative.overview: The visual language of the Driver Monitoring System is modeled after high-reliability modern flight deck telemetry: dark-mode by default, high-contrast, razor-sharp hierarchy, and designed for sub-second glanceable comprehension. When a vehicle is moving at highway speed, the driver's interface must communicate status unequivocally without demanding cognitive load or causing optical fatigue under day and night lighting.
keyCharacteristics: Zero Ambiguity Glancability: Telemetry metrics feature prominent numerical values paired with analog micro-bars.
Tonal Elevation Hierarchy: Depth is created via layered dark slate tones with subtle luminous glowing borders on alert states.
Calm at Rest, Assertive on Alarm: The UI remains subdued and non-distracting during safe driving, converting into a pulsing beacon only when safety thresholds are breached.

rules.name: The Rarity of Red Rule
rules.body: The Hazard Crimson (#EF4444) is strictly prohibited in decorative, branding, or non-hazardous contexts. Its appearance is a direct signal of active safety intervention.

rules.name: The Tabular Metric Rule
rules.body: Every real-time floating-point number (EAR, MAR, Yaw, Pitch) MUST use monospaced figures to guarantee zero layout shifts during continuous inference rendering.

rules.name: The Signal-Responsive Glow Rule
rules.body: Glowing colored shadows are never persistent; they exist solely as dynamic state reactions to active warnings or primary touch interactions.

dos: Do maintain dark cockpit palette (#0F172A background) across all authenticated screens to preserve nighttime driver night-vision.
Do format real-time metric floats with exactly three decimal places inside font-mono containers.
Do pair color changes with iconography so colorblind drivers never miss an alert state.
Do ensure critical alarm sirens can be toggled or tested on-demand via audio context activation.
donts: Don't introduce bright white background containers in the driver cockpit interface.
Don't use Red (#EF4444) for non-emergency UI decoration, illustrations, or secondary buttons.
Don't let live video or telemetry canvas elements shift layout when values transition between two-digit and three-digit percentages.
Don't use decorative serif fonts or novelty typefaces anywhere in the operational monitoring flow.
